stem: In triangle \(ABC\), the measure of angle \(A\) is \(48^{\circ}\). Sides \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{AC}\) are extended past \(B\) and \(C\) to points \(D\) and \(E\). Ray \(BP\) bisects angle \(CBD\), and ray \(CP\) bisects angle \(BCE\), as shown. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(BPC\)?
solution: Let the angles of the triangle at \(B\) and \(C\) be \(b\) and \(c\), with \(b + c = 180 - 48 = 132\).
The exterior angle at \(B\) is \(180 - b\), so angle \(PBC = 90 - \frac{b}{2}\). Likewise, angle \(PCB = 90 - \frac{c}{2}\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(ang('B','A','C')-48)<0.1
assert abs(ang('C','B','P')-ang('P','B','D'))<0.1 and abs(ang('B','C','P')-ang('P','C','E'))<0.1
ans=Rational(180-48,2)
assert abs(ang('B','P','C')-ans)<0.1
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==66
